docs.title: Type Omega Dev Docs
docs.text:
Developer documentation for Type Omega (formerly GregTech Infinity Ascension), a GregTech modpack for Minecraft 1.20.1 built on GTCEu Modern, the GregTech Nexus Addon (GTNA) and TypeOmega Core.

This site is for people who build the pack: what it is trying to be, how decisions are made, and how to write code for it. Players should start at the modpack repository.

Community: Discord · questions, bug reports and playtesting.

Section What you find there Vision The design pillars, what each tier is about, and the rules for each game system Governance Approved decisions and how releases work Development Building the mods, code conventions and GameTests

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
Repository Role TypeOmega The modpack: configs, KubeJS, quests, manifest TypeOmegaCore Core mod: pack machines, chemistry slices, megastructures GregTech-Nexus-Addon GTNA: large machines, Nexus energy network, endgame multiblocks Agronomica Crop breeding mod (early development)

Policies that apply everywhere live in the organisation's .github repository: Code of Conduct, AI policy and contribution guidelines.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text: These rules apply to every mod in the organisation.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
• Keep files small. A Java class over ~500 lines should be split by responsibility. A test class over ~800 lines should be split by system (multiblock/<machine>/, compat/<mod>/).
  • No giant log files. Do not keep growing ledgers, journals or "continuity" files in the repository. History belongs in git commits and changelogs; decisions belong in the decisions page.
  • One topic per pull request.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• Write comments only at key points: a non-obvious rule, a balance number with its reason, a workaround for another mod, a mixin target. Code that explains itself gets no comment.
  • No comments that repeat the code, no commented-out code, no "added by…", no TODOs without an issue.
  • Key comments are written in English, Portuguese and Chinese, so any developer can understand why the code is there:
// EN: Bees only open in GregTech machines; the Productive Bees centrifuge is removed.
// PT: O comb só abre em máquinas GT; a centrífuga do Productive Bees foi removida.
// ZH: 蜂巢只能在格雷科技机器中处理；已移除 Productive Bees 的离心机。

docs.title: Languages
docs.text:
• Every name a player can see ships in en_us, pt_br and zh_cn in the same commit. A GameTest fails when one is missing.
  • Commit messages, changelogs and public docs are in English.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Content (machines, recipes, materials) lives in Java. KubeJS only removes or blocks recipes.
  • Multiblock tooltips use MultiblockTooltip.builder() of TypeOmega Lib in the GTNH layout (D-410), without a structure section or a pollution line (D-431); only the modes and the "Supports ...!" line are read from the GTCEu pattern by GtceuPatterns, and nothing hides behind Shift (D-428).
  • The author's textures and art are never replaced without the author's approval.

docs.title: GameTests
docs.text:
Every mod runs its GameTests in CI with ./gradlew runGameTestServer. The rules below follow the Horizon-QA principles used by GTNH.

  1. Functional tests, not mocks. Place real blocks and run the real machine.
  2. Mock supply, not validation. A test may give a machine its inputs any way it likes, but it never bypasses recipe logic.
  3. Wait on state, not ticks. Tick counts are only timeouts.
  4. Negative tests matter. For every new multiblock, add at least a "forms" test and a test that it does not form, or does not run, when it should not.
  5. Leave no trace. Remove any block placed outside the template, and never leave a synthetic recipe registered.
  6. Failures explain themselves. The message says what went in, what was expected and what happened.

docs.title: Sweep tests
docs.text:
Each mod has tests that sweep over everything it registers, so new content is checked the day it is added:

  • every multiblock forms from its own preview;
  • no GT recipe has an empty input or output, or a duration of 0;
  • every machine tooltip builds without a raw translation key;
  • every name exists in en_us, pt_br and zh_cn.

docs.title: Filtering GameTests
docs.text:
Mods that depend on TypeOmega Lib get GameTest filtering automatically via -Dtypeomega.tests=<terms> (GameTestFilter), matching comma-separated terms (case-insensitive substring match) against the method name, simple class name or batch name.

To pass -Ptests=... from Gradle, expose the property in your gameTestServer run configuration:

runs {
    gameTestServer {
        systemProperty('typeomega.tests', project.findProperty('tests') ?: '')
    }
}

docs.title: Heavy batch
docs.text: Slow or expensive tests (such as auto-build sweeps) should be marked with batch = TestBatches.HEAVY or @HeavyTest (on a method or class). Heavy tests are excluded by default and from normal filtered runs; they only run when heavy or all is passed.

docs.title: Fast workflow vs. final commit
docs.text:
During active development, filter down to the area you are working on:

./gradlew runGameTestServer -Ptests=nanoforge
./gradlew runGameTestServer -Ptests=nanoforge,tooltip
./gradlew runGameTestServer -Ptests=heavy

Before the final commit, always run the full suite including heavy tests:

./gradlew runGameTestServer -Ptests=all

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: The pack targets under 4 GB of RAM on servers and clients, and Android through the Amethyst launcher. Every optimization goes in with numbers from before and after, measured the same way.

docs.title: How we measure
docs.text:
tools/perf_bench.py in the modpack boots a dedicated server with exactly the locked mods (median of 3 runs) and records:

Metric Meaning wall_s Seconds from launch until the server is ready done_s Minecraft's own "Done (…)" time (world preparation) heap_after_gc_mb Live heap after a forced full GC (class histogram) mspt Average server tick time while /typeomegalib bench keeps a grid of GT machines running

The client side uses tools/client_bench.py: it joins a test world on the Prism instance with a given heap limit and records live heap, RSS and out-of-memory errors.

python3 tools/perf_bench.py my-label --runs 3 --extra DIR_WITH_CANDIDATE_JARS \
    --tick gtceu:lv_electric_furnace:2000:minecraft:raw_iron --replace gtna=path/to/gtna.jar --off gtcovers

Results are appended to ~/MineProjects/GTIA-arquivo/perf/<label>.jsonl. Profiles use JFR (--jvm "-XX:StartFlightRecording=...").

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Measure before writing the optimization; profile to find the real hotspot.
  2. Keep the optimization switchable (Ascension Optimizer features can be turned off in config/ascopt-mixins.properties).
  3. Run the mod's full GameTest suite after the change.
  4. Record the numbers in the commit, the changelog and this page.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
All mods target Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.4.x, Java 17 and build with Gradle (ModDevGradle legacy Forge).

git clone https://github.com/Type-Omega/TypeOmegaCore.git
cd TypeOmegaCore
./gradlew build
./gradlew runGameTestServer -PtypeOmegaDevOptionalDependencies=true
Command What it does ./gradlew runClient Starts a development client ./gradlew runData Regenerates data (recipes, models, en_us.json) ./gradlew runGameTestServer Runs every GameTest headlessly and exits with an error on failure ./gradlew spotlessApply Formats the code

TypeOmegaCore needs GTNA and AE2 at runtime. Without them, pass -PtypeOmegaDevOptionalDependencies=true so the test server can start.

docs.title: Dev runtime flags (TypeOmegaCore)
docs.text: Flag What it does -PtypeOmegaDevOptionalDependencies=true Loads optional pack dependencies (Productive Bees, Ad Astra, AE2 WCWT, AE2 Wireless Terminals) at dev runtime and sets integration_mandatory=false -PtypeOmegaDevFtbTeams=false Disables FTB Teams in dev runtime (loaded by default) to test solo fallback paths -PtypeOmegaDevPlaytest=true Loads client playtest mods (FTB Chunks, AE2 WCWT, AE2 Wireless Terminals) for runClient -Ptests=<terms> Filters runGameTestServer by method, class or batch (heavy or all for heavy tests; see GameTests)

docs.title: The modpack
docs.text: The pack is managed with packwiz. manifest/full.lock.json is the source of truth: tools/pack.py lock|fetch, then tools/packwiz_sync.py. Quests are generated from quests-src/ with tools/questgen.py build and checked with tools/questgen.py check.

docs.title: Organisation Maven
docs.text:
Released mod jars are published at https://type-omega.github.io/maven/ (no login needed). The maven repository checks for new GitHub releases every 6 hours and keeps the newest 5 versions of each artifact.

repositories {
    maven { url = 'https://type-omega.github.io/maven/' }
}
dependencies {
    modCompileOnly("com.raishxn.gtna:gtna:0.6.0") { transitive = false }
}

TypeOmegaCore compiles against GTNA from there. To compile against a local GTNA build instead, pass -PgtnaApiJar=/path/to/gtna.jar. To publish a new mod, add it to artifacts.json in the maven repository.

docs.title: TypeOmega Lib
docs.text: TypeOmega Lib (com.typeomega:typeomega-lib) is the shared library used across Type Omega mods. Below are the client and testing utilities added in 0.8.1–0.8.4.

docs.title: GTNH-Style Paginated Tooltips
docs.text:
Package: com.typeomega.lib.tooltip.paging (TooltipPaging, TooltipPager, EmiModLine).

Long item tooltips are split into pages when they exceed the available screen height at the current GUI scale or exceed 20 body rows, even on tall screens:

  • Whole sections per page: TooltipPager breaks pages at separators and section headers (softBreakBefore) and spreads lines as evenly as possible across the fewest pages. A section is only split if that section alone is taller than one page.
  • Header: Line 0 (the item name) repeats at the top of every page.
  • Navigation: Press Tab (Shift+Tab goes back) or use Ctrl + mouse wheel.
  • EMI integration: Paging runs in ItemTooltipEvent on the render thread when a screen is open, so tooltips hovered in EMI's item list are paged while EMI's background search index still sees all lines. EmiModLine automatically drops our trailing italic blue mod-name line when EMI is configured to append its own (appendModId and appendItemModId), avoiding duplicate mod names.

To opt a mod's items in during client setup (already enabled by default for typeomega, typeomegalib, gtna and agronomica):

TooltipPaging.enable("mymod");

docs.title: UI Module
docs.text:
Package: com.typeomega.lib.ui.

  • FlowArrowWidget: Animates arrows or pipes painted directly in the panel's pixel-art texture without modifying the art asset. Any layout mark whose id starts with flow_ (flow_right, flow_left, flow_down, flow_up) turns white pixels (0xFFFFFFFF) inside the mark into a grey-to-white fill cycling every 2000 ms.
  • InfoLinesWidget: Draws recipe and machine info lines. When a line is wider than the panel width, it is automatically scaled down (scale = room / width) so text never overflows the frame.
  • Unused slot removal (IllustratedRecipeUI): When building a recipe page, IllustratedRecipeUI.removeUnusedSlots removes any item or fluid slots defined in the panel layout that the current recipe does not use, showing only active inputs and outputs.

docs.title: Shared HUD Editor
docs.text:
Package: com.typeomega.lib.ui.hud (MoveableHud, HudRegistry, HudEditorScreen, HudPositionStore, HudClient).

All mods register their overlays in one shared registry so the player uses a single keybind (H by default, under the TypeOmega Lib key category) to open HudEditorScreen, toggle HUDs on or off, and drag them to persisted screen-percentage positions (0..100%) stored in config/typeomegalib-huds.json.

To register a HUD during client setup:

HudRegistry.register(new MoveableHud() {
    @Override public String id() { return "mymod:my_hud"; }
    @Override public Component displayName() { return Component.translatable("hud.mymod.my_hud"); }
    @Override public int width() { return 140; }
    @Override public int height() { return 48; }
    @Override public boolean isEnabled() { return MyConfig.hudEnabled; }
    @Override public void setEnabled(boolean enabled) { MyConfig.setHudEnabled(enabled); }
    @Override public void render(GuiGraphics graphics, int x, int y, int width, int height) {
        // draw HUD contents at (x, y)
    }
});

Optional overrides on MoveableHud:

  • shouldRenderInGame() — extra visibility condition on top of isEnabled() (ignored in HudEditorScreen so enabled HUDs can still be positioned before data arrives).
  • defaultXPercent() / defaultYPercent() — initial anchor percentages before the player moves the HUD (default 5, 5).

docs.title: Approved decisions
docs.text:
Product decisions have stable IDs (D-NNN) that are never reused. Only the pack author approves a decision; a proposal is not a decision because it appears in a document. Revoked decisions keep their ID and are marked as revoked.

Older entries are kept as written and use the project's former names (GT:IA, GTIA, GTIACore, GTIA Lib; now Type Omega, TypeOmegaCore, TypeOmega Lib).

This page lists the approved product decisions that shape development. Internal drafts, audits and studies are not published.

ID Decision D-141 Greenhouse and Pyrolyse Oven arrive early in MV. The Greenhouse is optional and starts sun-dependent; the Pyrolyse Oven is strongly recommended but does not gate HV. D-221 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Vertical, generated quest book (questgen.py) with chapters per tier, fixed meaning for side lanes and shapes per role, and automatic checks. D-226 No research tree. The pack is about building and running megafactories. D-227 Megafactory in depth and width. In the first 20 hours, new machines every session. 1–2 rebuilds per tier. The factory goes wherever the player wants. D-228 Processing lines grow with the tier (Steam 2–3, LV/MV 4–6, HV/EV 6–10, IV+ 10+), with by-products, closed loops, waste treatment and branching mid-line. D-229 Real chemistry without requiring a PhD, in the order Steam wood/coal and lime → LV chlor-alkali and steel → LV/MV Bayer + Hall-Héroult → MV Contact, Haber-Bosch + Ostwald, Solvay → HV refining. D-230 Resources: wells with purity, infinite sources per tier, planetary gases, renewables as real routes, mobs only from the Slaughterhouse, rare elements only as by-products. D-231 Energy: real fuel lines, heat as a resource, chemical and thermal storage, losses on wireless energy. D-232 Superseded by D-340. Logistics: no throughput limits, AE2 storage at the end of LV and autocrafting in MV, no Create. D-233 Multiblocks: upgrades by parts, Mega for everything, no limit, parallelism explained with numbers, modules through hatches and the GTNA module system, no luck-based progression. D-234 Danger: GTCEu explosions and hazards, cleanrooms, inert atmospheres, safety gear. D-237 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Grind is solved with more factory. Own recipes for key items plus automatic shortcut checks. Modes chosen at world creation and locked. D-238 Chosen unique ideas: process conditions, two routes per molecule, closed loops, wells with purity, heat as a resource, factory dimension, planetary gases, rare elements only as by-products. D-244 Standard multiblock tooltips in the GTNA format: a real fact, then Main Function, Auxiliary Module and Running Requirements. D-246 Better versions of the real-chemistry multiblocks (rotary kiln, membrane cell…) come from IV/LuV onwards. D-254, D-256 GTIA Rules: Journey, Normal and Custom presets; 44 rules in 7 groups; rules never change registries. D-257 Crafting Chain (separate mod) replaces Fabricate. D-259 Bees arrive in HV through Productive Bees with its base recipes removed. D-260 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Agronomica: our own crop mod, separate repository, LGPL-3.0. D-261 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Ore boost with a reagent: 1 crushed + 1 leaf + reagent → 3 purified. D-262 GTIA Lib is the org's foundation library (depends on GTCEu); GTNA, GTIACore and Agronomica require it. GTOLib ideas are reimplemented from scratch, never copied. D-263 Ascension Optimizer (ascopt, no GT dependency): spawn chunks 441 → 25; server ready in 31 s instead of 47 s. D-264 Client uses ModernFix dynamic_resources; LeanObject is server-only (menu heap −37 %). D-265 EMI multiblock previews built on demand and GTNA shape cache in SoftReference: EMI reload 20.6 → 12.2 s, client runs with 1.5 GB. D-266 Draconium belongs to GTNA only; GTIACore's copy was removed. D-267 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Agronomica core: crop sticks, four Steam/LV crops, Growth/Gain/Resistance (soft cap above 20), cross-breeding with mutations, NPK soil and fertilisers. D-268 HV bee line: all Productive Bees recipes and nests disabled; caged metal bees come from the Chemical Reactor, the Industrial Apiary (HV–UV) makes combs, combs give a small dust or, with HCl, purified ore. D-269 Recommended client flags: G1 periodic GC with free ratios 10–30 % and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2; client RSS 6.0 → 4.4 GB with the same live heap. D-270 No batched @Synced for now: a player next to 500 working LV furnaces receives about 1.3 KB/s; LDLib sync is not a network bottleneck. D-275 HV quest chapter v6 approved: every dependency has a recipe reason checked against a GTNH 2.9 / GTO 0.6 quest atlas; tier machines are side quests unless a goal needs them; the circuit ladder (HV → EV → IV) lives inside the tier; the EV circuit comes right after the Cleanroom because HV multiblocks need it. D-276 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Start–MV quest chapters v7 in game, built like HV v6: recipe reason on every dependency, tier motor and turbine as central hubs, LV motor before the LV turbine, separate components, MV PVC board and CPU chip line, HV gets an HV steam turbine. Hidden lines use FTB's per-quest flags on either side; crossings and long lines are notes in questgen check. D-277 Rocket Assembler (HV): 15 × 15 × 20 launch complex (twin stepped service towers, scaffold, umbilicals, crane bridge, flame trench), own casing with LDLib connected textures; the tier 1 rocket and its Ad Astra parts are made through GT and Ad Astra's own recipes for them are dropped. D-278 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Mode-only quests: GTIACore tags the player gtia_journey or gtia_normal from the world preset (Custom counts as Normal); a hidden modes chapter turns the tag into an FTB Quests stage, and quests marked with a mode stay hidden in the other one. The Start chapter's strong tool rewards become the Journey Starting Kit; Normal gets steel tools and an LV prospector. D-279 Organ system ported from GTO 0.6 into GTIACore: 9 organ types × tiers 0–4, steel/fairy/mechanical wings, Organ Modifier screen (9 organ + 8 wing slots), organs kept in persisted player data. Effects as in GTO (leg speed scaled to +10/30/60/100 %, +5 armor and toughness per set tier, +4 reach, liver and lung perks, no hunger at set 3, flight at set 4). Ad Astra planets hurt players below set tier (t−1)/2+1 (Moon and Mars: 1). GTO assembler recipes; phantom membranes replace Botania in the cheap wings. GTO's "nano wall" is left out (GTOLib only). D-280 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). GTIA Rules grow from 44 to 52 for parity with GTO Rules: rubber tree chance, infinite bedrock fluids, require GT tools (restart), material hazards, extra regeneration (food threshold and strength), planets need organs, organ cost. GTO rules without a GTIA mechanic stay out (see the table below). D-281 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). MV/HV chemistry lines: Ostwald Converter (MV, cobalt oxide gauze; HV platinum gauze), Claus Unit, Kroll Reactor and Siemens Reactor (HV), Czochralski boule from 16 polysilicon in the EBF. Real stoichiometry and closed loops (NO, Mg/Cl₂, HCl). D-282 Main menu with FancyMenu 3.9.12 (Konkrete, Melody) instead of PackMenu: animated emblem plus the author's text logo recoloured in purple, animated pixel-art space-factory background, buttons Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Mods, Settings, Quit and Discord. D-283 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Quest book highlight images: isometric renders of 19 multiblocks from the real textures (modpack/tools/iso_render.py). The Moon quest is a dimension task and the reachability model knows Ad Astra's own Moon blocks, so no lunar quest is pending.

GTIA's own chemistry rules (54 rules in all): catalyst wear (Normal: 1 % chance per run that the Ostwald/Claus catalyst wears out; Journey: never) and heat recovery (Journey: 1.5× the steam of the chemistry plants). Organ textures redrawn; Organ Modifier screen shows the slots on a body outline with an effect readout. Main menu: one row of four textured buttons (Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Settings, Quit) and a Discord icon. D-285 The Android .mrpack ships from 0.1.0-dev-5: Modrinth links where the exact file exists, every CurseForge-only jar inside the pack with the author's permission (owners informed; removed at once on request). Built locally with tools/mrpack.py and attached to the release. D-286 Space age direction: the station lives in Ad Astra's orbit, starts in HV and is modular (a core plus connectors and modules that grow the station, with GTIA-only modules); the extreme-gravity destination is an Ad Astra planet (datapack). Three community stations (ABFielder "Space Station fiop", Toppat Orbital Station, Icarus), cleared for use by the author, replace Ad Astra's default station structures with GTNA ABS casings and Ad Astra plating, doors and lamps. Fouling and vein purity rules are approved. D-287 Quest book layout in the GTNH way: tools/quest_layout.py places Steam, LV, MV, HV, Agriculture and Bees in dependency columns ordered to minimise crossings, with leaf quests in a ring around the quest they hang from and large collections as a grid block; tier-wide hubs (7+ dependents) do not place quests and their lines are hidden; long lines, lines over a quest and lines crossing twice per line are hidden. Every dependency stays (reachability). Visible crossings: Steam 102 → 5, LV 78 → 4, MV 35 → 6, HV 31 → 4. Book theme: opaque dark background, thick red/green lines. Era banners as chapter images. D-288 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Creating a world whose preset changes a startup rule asks for a restart first, like GTO's difficulty: "Save and Quit" writes the rules, closes the game and keeps the choice for the next create-world screen. Opening a saved world with other startup values asks too (Save and Quit / Play anyway). D-289 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Agriculture (21 quests) and Bees (13 quests) chapters in the Systems group. New recipes for the empty Bee Cage, the Honey Treat (Mixer) and the Greenhouse controller, which had none; a GameTest now checks that every GTIA machine has a recipe. D-290 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Mode quests are visible from the start in worlds of their mode: the Starting Kits complete with their Start step's task, and one opening quest per mode explains what it changes. D-291 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). The Start splits GTO-style into Welcome (reading, the world's mode, rules, community, EMI and Crafting Chain tips) and a step-by-step Start that snakes from the first log to the first Coke, with tips next to the steps that need them; the author's 29 quests keep ids, text, tasks and rewards. Steam supplies become per-mode kits. Tips in LV, MV and HV. Multiblock Goals chapter after GTNH's: all 254 multiblocks in a grid, columns by family, rows by the voltage their controller recipe needs, text from each mod's own tooltip. D-292 Multiblock renders leave the quest map and quest text (EMI's preview stays, press R); the era banner sits in the free space nearest the chapter's entry quest. D-293 Steam, LV, MV and HV take the GTNH 2.9 chapter structure: a quest with a GTNH equivalent goes to its place, GTIA-only quests sit next to the quest they depend on, no quests added; dependencies thinned by the reachability check to 1–2 per quest. Every chapter has its own low-contrast pixel-art background tile: Steam bronze, LV grey, MV blue, HV light steel, EV light purple, IV dark blue; Welcome dark brick, Start stone, Agriculture farmland, Bees honeycomb, Energy coils, Wireless circuit traces, reference chapters a neutral grid. D-294 Partly revised by D-345 (Pyrolyse Oven log recipes are back). No competing chemistry routes. 47 GTCEu/GTNA direct syntheses that skipped GTIA's chemistry lines are removed in both modes: aluminium (bauxite, sapphire, kyanite, clay and aluminium sulfite electrolysis; the bauxite sludge chain), sulfuric acid, ammonia, nitric acid, membrane-less chlor-alkali, soda ash, titanium tetrachloride and its reduction outside the Kroll Reactor, quicklime, chemical ethylene (cracking stays) and log pyrolysis. By-products (ores, distillation, recycling, silicate decomposition) stay. The GTCEu silicon boule stays because the HV Siemens Reactor needs HV circuits, which need wafers. Quests that relied on the old routes now point to GTIA's plants. D-295 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Each Multiblock Goals quest gives a small pack of its row's metal (4 bronze, steel, aluminium, stainless steel, titanium or tungstensteel ingots; 2 of the LuV–UV metal; 1 neutronium), checked by the reachability tool. D-296 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Steam, LV, MV and HV go back to the v7 layout (each quest's own x/y) until the new GTNH layout is approved: the D-293 layout hid the lines of 36–58% of the quests in each chapter and left 15–29 quests per chapter with no line at all. D-297 The GTNH layout is redone by the generator around GTNH's hubs: checked GTIA↔GTNH pairs; where a GTIA quest takes a GTNH hub, the quests under it depend on it (implied dependencies only); a GTNH hub with no GTIA pair becomes a GTIA milestone quest (imported or checkmark); the GTNH grid is compacted; GTIA-only quests branch in straight rows; quests move before lines are hidden; sizes 1/2/3. Targets: no quest without a line, at most 10% with hidden lines, no overlaps or lines over quests. D-298 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Work moves to mechanics, processing lines and performance; the quest book comes last, before the public release. Changes target critical, specific points: GTCEu machines and multiblocks stay and get recipes with new materials, and a new machine is added only when no existing one can do the step. Alternative routes follow GTNH's model (for example three routes to aluminium ingots). D-299 Revoked by D-334. Nothing from GTNA or GTIA is removed (lines, recipe types, machines). Late GTNA machines are gated by their controller recipe: the Integrated Ore Processor around IV/LuV, the PCB Factory after LuV. D-300 Revoked by D-397 (Type Omega). Four Type Omega creative tabs: Machines; Multiblocks and Megastructures; Materials and Items; Blocks and Casings. (4) The Crafting Station works like the Tinkers' Construct station of GTNH: the grid is kept in the block (dropped when broken), containers on all six sides are tabs (a double chest counts once, another station never), shift-click on the result fills the neighbour's stacks before the player's, items move neighbour to player and player to the open tab's neighbour, an item brought from a neighbour goes back to it, and a button dumps the grid. D-434 Renders of the GTNA original multiblocks. Machines without a render come first, then the upgrades of the existing ones. The Nexus ME Hypercore gets a holographic core: one cube per crafting co-processor in orbit, data streams to the CPU interface and a pulse while a crafting job runs. The Nexus Flux Matrix gets a plasma column; the Nexus Assembly Forge and the ME Storage also get renders, but these three wait because their structures may still change. Every GTNA machine render follows one client option with three levels, OFF, LOW and HIGH (client.machineRenders): OFF hides only the effects (parts taken out of the world, such as the Forge of Gods rings, keep drawing, and the Stellar Chamber keeps its gravity and sound), LOW halves the effect range and drops the costly passes. The Antimatter Collider Ring is brought to the Stellar Chamber's level, and the Kinetic Orbital Lance and the Dimensional Rift Gate get the upgrades of the render proposal. D-435 GTNH-style illustrated recipe screens. SH-Better-UI is a reference only (MIT; any ported code is credited). The screens live in a ui module of TypeOmega Lib on top of LDLib (0.7.0). Look: each recipe type has a pixel-art background of its process with the slots and tanks drawn into it, on the GTCEu bevelled grey, and under it Total EU, Usage with the tier colour, Time and the type's own fields. Mixed approach: .rtui files for fixed layouts, setRecipeUI for dynamic ones, and native EMI categories only for the GTNA originals, which have no GT recipe. First batch: Tokamak Fusion (core, start-up EU and ignition temperature from the constants) and EMI pages for the Antimatter Collider Ring, Dimensional Rift Gate, Kinetic Orbital Lance and Stellar Containment Chamber (rules read from their cores). The same widgets serve EMI and the machine GUI (the Tokamak gets a Fusion tab with the same screen). New art awaits the author's review. D-436 One mode, no world rules. Every Type Omega world uses the values of the former Normal preset. The whole rules system is removed: the screen, the create-world button, the /typeomega rules command, the Journey/Normal/Custom presets, gtia_rules.json, the restart screen and their texts. Everything that read a rule uses the fixed Normal value: maintenance from LV, no wireless steam hatch recipes (steam through pipes), steam and recipe balance at x1, the Normal GTCEu recipe and machine settings, 1% catalyst wear, organ cost x2, 100,000 negentropy with the ending on, extra regeneration from food 15. Old worlds with gtia_rules.json load without errors and ignore the file. GTNA steam tooltips show a variant label only when there is more than one variant, so they show a plain number. The quest book loses the hidden modes chapter, the mode quests and the Journey kits; the 0.0 and Welcome kits keep the Normal rewards with the same ids. Reinforces D-383/D-385; revokes the rules part of D-433, the per-mode split of D-427 and "the GTIA Rules stay" of D-343. D-437 New shapes for three GTNA multiblocks, chosen by the author. ME Storage: the "Data Conduit", an octagonal data duct on a titanium keel; each repeated slice holds 6 storage cores, 1 to 128 slices (768 cores at most, as before), one ME Storage Access Hatch on the 3×3 front panel. Nexus Flux Matrix: the "Tesla Coil", a wide steel base, the 7×7 capacitor column behind borosilicate glass, loose busbars and a 21-block discharge toroid; each repeated floor holds 25 capacitors, 2 to 30 floors (750 at most, the unlimited threshold); energy hatches only on the front and back 3×3 panels. Nexus Assembly Forge: the "Orbital Forge of Crossed Rings", a chamfered cross base, two crossed rings and an octahedral core on a europium spindle; hatches only on the 5×5 front panel, and the plain zirconia behind it counts toward the minimum of 20, so every panel slot can hold a hatch; lamps about 2 % of the blocks; nothing floats. Each machine has a formation GameTest and a negative one. D-438 The HV Tokamak produces EU every tick, like the fusion reactors: its recipes output 2 A (D-T) and 4 A (D-He3) of HV per tick instead of one lump per cycle. The structure needs exactly 4 HV Dynamo Hatches, one per amp of the strongest fuel, and the preview shows all four; the tooltip, the recipe screen and the code comments read the same constants. D-439 Nexus Terminal v2 (GTNA). The terminal adopts the scan → plan → execute architecture and the functions of the gt_shanhai Ultimate Terminal (LGPL-3.0), rewritten in GTNA style and credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md where the code stays close. The item and the planner live in GTNA; the screens live in the TypeOmega Lib ui module (D-435). First batch: a reusable build plan, batched ME extraction through the AE2 API (no reflection), cached selections and candidates, one setBlock per block, per-tick placement (instant up to about 4096 cells, above that a server job with a progress bar and cancel), a read-only scan with coloured boxes in the world, a Materials tab with "Request from ME", a report, safe replacement, full disassembly, a hatch plan and a new four-tab screen (Build, Tiers, Hatches, Materials) in the GTNH look. Replacing a block or tier happens directly, without confirmation, but returns the old block and rolls back if placing fails. Disassembly sends blocks to the ME first, then to the inventory, and refuses if they do not fit. Hatch placement keeps its limits and gains a per-function plan (type and tier). The ME link has no range or dimension limit. Missing items with a pattern are requested from AE automatically when building. Later (P2): ghost hologram, area mode. No keybinds. One item; ME functions need an ME network. Fluids in structures only when a multiblock needs them. D-440 Nexus Terminal "Engineering Console" (GTNA). The terminal window becomes a console: numbered steps (structure, tiers, hatches, materials), the step page and a fixed action bar (scan, build, cancel, report); a Machines tab lists multiblocks within 32 blocks; a Saved Structures tab stores a built structure under a name and pastes it onto another controller of the same machine. Tiers can be swapped family by family. The last three follow ideas of GregTech Terminals (BgameXL, MIT), credited in GTNA's THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. D-441 Omega QA lives in its own repository (Type-Omega/Omega-QA, mod id omegaqa), like GTNH's Horizon-QA. The QA kit (GameTest DSL, rigs, sweeps, JUnit/JSON reports, perf benches, QA wand, AE2/EMI/FTB bridges, SPIs) left TypeOmega Lib, which keeps only shared gameplay code. Players never load QA tooling, and it changes at a different pace than the lib. D-442 AE2 pieces from GTOCore are reimplemented in the core, not copied: ME Interface (II)-(V), Acceleration Card (II)-(V), ME Requestable Input Bus/Hatch and the wireless ME network, with GTOCore's mechanics and numbers written from scratch (GTOCore is PolyForm Noncommercial, so it is a reference only). AE2 Wireless Terminals joins the pack. The wireless terminal is AE2 WCWT (MIT), not GTOCore's; the core adds automatic pattern upload by recipe type, reimplemented from ExtendedAE Plus (LGPL-3.0, credited) without needing it. ME Placement Tool is in the pack. Copying the code was rejected because it would tie those files to a noncommercial licence. D-443 The Kardashev Meter stays a single block in the first chapter with its current recipe, and gets its own screen (Summary, History, Sources tabs) plus a HUD toggle like the Flux Matrix. The official K stays the per-tier table of D-380; the screen also shows the power in watts and Sagan's K as an extra line. Wireless networks, boilers and local GTCEu generators (Tokamak included) count, with no double counting through Wireless Dynamo Hatches. Six hours of history. The HUD editor moves from GTNA to TypeOmega Lib so all HUDs share one editor and key. D-444 The wireless ME network of GTLCore (LGPL-3.0, ported with credit) goes into GTNA and replaces the small connector/configurator the core got in D-442: a Wireless Network Core with its own screen, a binding tool with a network picker on a key (works from any slot, Curios included), auto-binding when a block is sneak-placed, any AE2 target as a member, team-owned bindings. GTLCore's extra terminals come later. D-445 Megastructures v2. Visual direction "dark hull and light": charcoal palette with one accent per megastructure, emissive parts, no new shader, same sizes. 41 new blocks (37 exclusive, 4 shared), delivered in waves; pilot on Yggdrasil, Nidavellir and Star Lifter. The controller sits on a 7×5 service deck fixed to a static part of the structure at mid height; the separate station and bridge are removed; the 3×3 hatch area stays. Each hull is researched from the previous megastructure's hull, at the controller's tier, with a high yield per craft. D-446 Megastructures are converted from the original 3D models of Gigastructural Engineering & More and Sparble's Stellar Hyperconstructs, phase by phase, provisionally until the creators grant permission (requested in parallel; otherwise back to own models). Mod textures are not used. The Neutronium Gigaforge joins as a second megastructure that feeds the Nidavellir Hyperforge; both require a neutron star, pulsar or magnetar. The Penrose Sphere becomes a second megastructure on the HRAE-MC's black hole. The Assembly Yard gets six-fold symmetry with its six plasma pumps. Birch World becomes a habitat; the Suprashell keeps time dilation. The Planetary Seeder Nexus, Equatorial Shipyard and Basement Gateway join in waves after the Nidavellir, HRAE-MC and Yard fixes. As built: the Seeder Nexus is a cheaper Yggdrasil companion (greenhouse and biomass recipes; the Seeder-to-Yggdrasil upgrade path is deferred); the Basement Gateway works around any star and receives the matter of a Solar System Disintegrator in the same system. D-447 The Nexus Terminal screen takes the futuristic purple-and-black look of GTCEu Terminals, with the same functions as before. The look is a selectable theme of TypeOmega Lib's ToolWindow (other tools keep the grey GTNH look); frames and buttons are drawn in code, with no 9-slice PNGs; Dismantle stays a toggle in step 1 with a red warning and a quick preview; the window keeps its fixed 420×236 size. D-448 Megastructure rendering: the block structure stays what the player builds and what forms the machine; once formed, the client draws the original 3D model over it with our own material (no mod textures), moving parts and emissive parts, to come as close to 1:1 as possible. Provisional until the creators grant permission, like D-446. Tested on one megastructure first.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Channel How it is made Who it is for Nightly Every push to main of the modpack replaces the nightly pre-release Testers who want the latest build dev / pre / alpha The Package workflow run by hand with a tag such as 0.1.0-dev-5, 0.1.0-pre-1 or 0.1.0-alpha Testers following a milestone beta The same workflow with a -beta tag The first channel published as stable

Only the newest release of each group is kept (the newest beta and the newest dev/pre/alpha); the nightly is never removed by a versioned release.

Changelogs and release notes are written in English. Mods (TypeOmegaCore, GTNA, Agronomica) release on their own and the pack pins exact versions with SHA-256 in manifest/full.lock.json.

docs.title: Mobile
docs.text: The pack targets Android through the Amethyst launcher with the .mrpack build, the same way GTNH supports mobile; the player guide is docs/MOBILE.md. The .mrpack is built by tools/mrpack.py (--test embeds the CurseForge-only mods, for private tests only). Only the official .mrpack with default configs is supported; mobile bugs use the mobile issue form.

docs.title: AE2 in Type Omega
docs.text: Type Omega extends Applied Energistics 2 with higher-tier interfaces, faster acceleration cards and automatic pattern upload, all implemented from scratch in TypeOmega Core (D-442).

docs.title: Tiered ME Interfaces
docs.text:
ME Interface (II)–(V) expand on the plain AE2 ME Interface (tier 0). Every tier above the plain interface has 36 config slots and 36 storage slots, and is available as both a full block (me_interface_ii–v) and a cable part (cable_me_interface_ii–v).

Tier Slot multiplier Recipe circuit II ×4,096 MV III ×262,144 EV IV ×16,777,216 LuV V ×1,073,741,824 UV

In-place upgrade: Sneak + right-clicking a lower-tier interface (including the plain AE2 interface) with a higher-tier one of the same form (block on block, part on part) replaces it in place. Configuration, stored contents, installed upgrade cards, priority and custom name are preserved, and the old interface is returned to the player.

docs.title: Tiered Acceleration Cards
docs.text:
Acceleration Card (II)–(V) are crafted from four plain AE2 Acceleration Cards around a circuit of the tier's voltage. Each tier is worth 8× the previous one, starting from the plain AE2 card (×1).

Tier Equivalent AE2 cards Recipe circuit II ×8 EV III ×64 LuV IV ×512 UV V ×4,096 UEV

Where they apply: Tiered Acceleration Cards speed up AE2 and ExtendedAE transfer machines:

  • Import and Export Buses (operations per tick)
  • ME IO Port (3 card slots) and Extended IO Port (5 card slots, items moved per tick)

The machine's card slot limit is shared across all tiers, counting the highest tiers first. Each installed card contributes its multiplier toward the machine's scaling table (table(cards) × (sum of multipliers) / cards).

docs.title: Automatic Pattern Upload
docs.text:
When encoding a processing pattern after transferring a recipe from EMI or JEI, the encoded pattern is automatically uploaded to the matching ME Pattern Provider (or Extended Pattern Provider) on the same ME network instead of waiting in the terminal:

  • Works in both AE2's Pattern Encoding Terminal and AE2 WCWT (AE2 Wireless Comprehensive Work Terminal).
  • Matches the recipe type/category name against active pattern providers on the grid. An exact name match beats a partial substring match, and the matching provider name must be unique (otherwise the terminal reports no match or ambiguity).
  • Duplicate patterns already present in the target provider are skipped.
  • Hold Shift while pressing Encode to keep the pattern in the terminal instead of uploading it.

ExtendedAE Plus compatibility

Automatic pattern upload is reimplemented from ExtendedAE Plus (LGPL-3.0, credited in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md) without requiring it in the pack. If ExtendedAE Plus is installed, TypeOmega Core automatically disables its own upload hook so patterns are not sent twice.

docs.title: Pack AE2 Mods
docs.text:
Alongside AE2 and ExtendedAE, the pack includes:

  • AE2 Wireless Terminals (applied-energistics-2-wireless-terminals)
  • AE2 WCWT (ae2-wcwt, MIT) — the wireless crafting/work terminal used in the pack
  • ME Placement Tool
  • ME Requestable Input Bus/Hatch and the wireless ME network (D-442, implemented in TypeOmega Core)

docs.title: Kardashev Meter
docs.text:
In development

The Kardashev Meter rework (D-443) is currently in development. This page documents the approved design.

The Kardashev Meter (D-443) measures a team's total power generation on the Kardashev scale.

docs.title: Block and Screen
docs.text:
• Single block: Stays a single block in the first chapter with its existing recipe.
  • Dedicated screen: Opens a UI with three tabs — Summary, History and Sources — plus a HUD toggle (similar to the Flux Matrix).
  • Scale and readouts:
  • The official K value uses the per-tier table from D-380 (1 A of each type's first tier is the integer: EV = 1, ZPM = 2, UEV = 3, OpV = 4; 8 EU/t = 0; linear in log4(EU/t) in between; 10-minute average, megastructure ceiling, tracked per team).
  • The screen also shows total power in watts and Sagan's K as an extra line.
  • History: Keeps 6 hours of history.

docs.title: Counted Sources
docs.text:
Power generation is aggregated across:

  • Wireless energy networks
  • Boilers
  • Local GTCEu generators (including the Tokamak)

Power flowing through Wireless Dynamo Hatches is not double-counted.

docs.title: HUD
docs.text: The Kardashev Meter HUD uses TypeOmega Lib's shared HUD editor, so all mod HUDs share one drag editor, one keybind and one position config file.

docs.title: Design pillars
docs.text: Type Omega is GregTech about building and running megafactories, on a Kardashev-scale arc: from the first steam machine to planetary, stellar and galactic engineering. It sits between GTNH, GregTech Odyssey and GregTech Leisure: GTNH's power options and detailed tooltips, GTO's fast early game and humour, GTL's clean pack without magic, and none of the free endgame items of GTL's modified editions.

docs.title: The ten pillars (D-333)
docs.text:
1. Kardashev scale. Eras are named after it; the endgame has Mega and Hyper blocks, Dyson spheres and Matrioshka brains.
  2. Survival is never a requirement. No dungeons, mob farming, food systems or exploration gates. Vanilla hunger.
  3. Mining without punishment. Good tools early, with Fortune that counts on GregTech ores; later the Entangled Miner.
  4. Easy building. FTB Ultimine from the start, the personal dimension in Steam, building gadgets and a multiblock builder.
  5. Early AE2. Storage and first automation in MV, refinement in HV.
  6. Space with purpose. Each destination has resources that make sense; visit once, then automate it by data.
  7. Many ways to make power, GTNH-style: steam turbines, combustion, semi-fluid, gas, then fission and nitrobenzene in EV.
  8. Wireless energy in HV–EV.
  9. Detailed multiblock tooltips like GTNH's, with a GTO-style joke line.
  10. Satisfactory feeling. Planning ratios and managing big factories, almost no survival.

docs.title: Working rules
docs.text:
• Grind is solved with more factory, never with more clicking.
  • Real chemistry, no PhD required, as recipes in GTCEu and GTNA machines. A custom multiblock is added only when no existing machine can do the job (D-335).
  • Nothing skips a tier. Shortcuts are same-tier kits and a vending machine, never free endgame items.
  • Every quest is reachable. A checker reads the pack's real recipes and fails the build if a quest asks for something you cannot make yet.

docs.title: What Type Omega does not do
docs.text:
• No magic mods.
  • No research tree, research points or production quotas as gates.
  • No ULV era. The campaign goes Start → Steam → LV → MV → HV → …
  • Aesthetics never count toward progress.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• Resource wells with purity, found by probe and worked by miners per tier.
  • Infinite sources per tier come from ordinary multiblocks (water pump, rock breaker…), never before Steam.
  • Renewables are real routes: agriculture → biomass → chemistry.
  • Mobs come only from the GTNA Industrial Slaughterhouse (LV), never from real mob farms.
  • Rare elements come only as by-products of specific lines.
  • Base chemicals have one real route each: Type Omega's plants (Bayer and Hall-Héroult for aluminium, Contact, Haber, Ostwald, diaphragm chlor-alkali, Solvay and lime kiln, Kroll, wood retort and still, catalytic dehydration). GTCEu's direct shortcuts to the same products are removed; by-products of other lines stay (D-294).

docs.title: Farming
docs.text:
• Crops (Agronomica): crop sticks, stats and cross-breeding, inspired by GTNH's CropsNH and Forestry, with Type Omega mechanics: NPK soil fed by the chemistry lines, climate controlled in the Greenhouse, pollination by bees, and phytomining (plants that recover metal from mining tailings).
  • Ore boost: 1 crushed ore + 1 leaf + a tier reagent → 3 purified ore, and the spent reagent goes back to be regenerated. The direct route (9 leaves → 1 dust) exists but is worse.
  • Bees (Productive Bees, from HV): base recipes removed; bees live as items inside the Industrial Apiary; combs only open in GregTech machines; new species from IV come from a mutation machine with a guaranteed result.
  • A crop or bee line yields per block about 10–25 % of the same tier's ore line. Its advantage is not needing a vein or a planet.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
• Every generator needs a real fuel line, with adjustable fuel blends.
  • Steam stays useful after the Steam age, and heat is a resource: exothermic reactions make steam.
  • Chemical and thermal storage, such as a molten-salt tank that stores heat and gives back steam.
  • Wireless energy has losses.

docs.title: Logistics
docs.text:
• No throughput limits as a mechanic. AE2 and wireless move things between areas.
  • No Create. Multiblock tanks and larger output hatches per tier.

docs.title: Danger
docs.text:
• Electrical explosions, hot and toxic fluids, radiation, with GTCEu's standard punishment.
  • Cleanrooms and inert atmospheres. Safety gear comes with corporate-humour quests.

docs.title: One mode
docs.text: Every world plays the same balance, the former Normal (D-436): maintenance from LV, steam through pipes, the same recipes, quests and rewards. There are no world rules and no difficulty presets.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
The full roadmap exists as a guide; a tier is only polished after the previous one has been played. Each chapter is drawn as a flowchart and approved before any quest is written.

Tier Line length Signature content Start — First tools, a Fortune pickaxe in the kit, FTB Ultimine Steam 2–3 steps Coke Oven wood and lime chemistry, fluxed steel, the GTNA large steam machines, personal dimension, first circuit by hand LV 4–6 Chlor-alkali in the Electrolyzer, real steelmaking, wood line to plastic, EBF and Aluminium, Entangled Miner MV 4–6 Gems and laser engraving, silicon and chips, stainless steel and Kanthal; Bayer, Hall-Héroult, Contact, Haber-Bosch and Solvay as recipes in GTCEu machines. AE2 storage and first automation. Agronomica crops in the GTNA Greenhouse HV 6–10 Full refining, AE2 refinement (Assembler Matrix), Flux Matrix wireless energy with losses, the Rocket Assembler and the Moon, bees EV 6–10 Full wireless energy, fission, nitrobenzene and gas turbines, Mars and Venus/Mercury, electric Void Miner per planet, zero gravity (in space or a ground simulator), the End IV+ 10+ Type Omega's own planets, Mega versions of the chemistry plants (rotary kiln, membrane cell, Hall-Héroult lines, double absorption)

Gases come from planets: CO₂ on Mars, H₂SO₄ on Venus. Rare elements only appear as by-products of specific lines.

docs.title: Beyond MAX: eras
docs.text:
Voltage stops at MAX (D-312). Each tier after it is an era: a rule of its own, a resource that is not EU, and a megastructure that opens it. Eras are a separate axis from voltage, so GTCEu, GTNA and GTO keep their 15 tiers. Each era has levels I to III, unlocked by milestones of that era instead of bigger circuits. How the game ends is up to the modpack.

Era Opened by Resource New rule Ψ Matrioshka Brain (D-311) Ψ, thought cycles Computed recipes: items made from patterns by spending Ψ; Landauer's limit caps Ψ per second Stellar Stellar Engine Momentum The Nexus System travels the galaxy; each region has its own elements Dimensional Ringworld Curvature Machines run inside pocket dimensions opened by the Rift Gate Causal Birch World Causal debt Negative-duration recipes: output first, the bill later; too much debt causes a paradox Final Hyperquasaric megaconstruction Negentropy A finite world stock that every recipe of the era spends

The table is a draft. Megastructure work is frozen until HV has been played (D-333).
